title: Profile stewardship automation and pinned-version rollback orchestration
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem statement:
Currently verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) are produced via an ad-hoc publish flow: manual verification notes, hand-edited metadata, and a one-time mail-merge style publish step. This causes stale pins, inconsistent cost attributions, and slow rollbacks when a new model or quantization profile regresses in latency or quality.

Goal:
Design and ship an automated stewardship workflow for Redwood-verified performance profiles that: (1) enforces signing and provenance, (2) attaches deterministic cost models and compatibility mappings, (3) supports canary publish + automated rollback orchestration, and (4) exposes an operational playbook and telemetry contracts so SRE/Runtime can act on regressions quickly.

Scope (this ticket):
- Define the publish artifact schema (signed manifest, cost model, KVs) and git-backed registry layout.
- Implement the publish orchestration spec (canary -> staggered expansion -> auto-rollback triggers).
- Attach telemetry contract for drift detection and rollout health dashboards.
- Create an operational runbook for rollback and emergency pin overrides.
- Deliver end-to-end integration plan with the runtime verifier pipeline (ENG) and Console UX (DX/Design).

Out of scope (future work):
- Full UI for manual profile editing (follow-on PM ticket).
- Multi-tenant billing export (separate billing project).
acceptance_criteria: Signed profile manifest schema documented and stored in git-backed registry (artifact + signature).
Automated publish pipeline that can: create canary publish, expand to full, and perform automated rollback within configured threshold windows.
Telemetry contract defined: list of metrics, threshold rules, and sample size requirements for latency/regression detection (doc + dashboard links).
Operational runbook that SRE/Runtime can follow to force-pin previous profile or execute emergency fallback (playbook checked into runbooks repo).
End-to-end integration test that simulates a regression and verifies rollback completes automatically and emits audit events.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ava T: Kickoff with Runtime and Research. Agreed to use git-backed manifests and PGP-like signing. Action: ENG to prototype signature verification in runtime.

2025-02-20 - Miguel R: Scoped publish orchestration: canary step is 5% traffic for 30 minutes, expand to 25%/1h then 100%/4h. Thresholds: 2x baseline p95 latency or 15% increase in error-rate triggers rollback. Need telemetry hookpoints from runtime.
2025-02-25 - Priya K (Security): KMS-attestation required for production publishes. We need an HSM-backed signing key + audit log. Filed ENG-ticket ENG-48211.
2025-02-28 - Design (Yuna L): Provided lightweight Console mocks for profile publish flow and emergency pin chooser. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/profile-publish-mockups
2025-03-01 - ENG (Samir V): Concern: automatic rollback must be idempotent and safe during dependent rollouts (dedicated pools). We'll add a quiesce window and per-customer override flag.
2025-03-03 - Ava T: PM review with Support. Added customer communication template and SLA note in runbook for customers on Dedicated/Private.
notes: Decision: store manifests as signed JSON + semantic versioned tag. Manifest fields include: model_id, model_version, quant_profile, perf_signals (p50/p95/throughput), cost_estimate_usd_per_1M_tokens, compatibility matrix, publish_author, signature, published_at.

Trade-offs discussed: aggressive auto-rollback reduces customer surprise but increases risk of oscillation. Mitigation: require two independent metric triggers or a manual approval gate for high-traffic profiles.
Follow-ups: PM to open a UI ticket for manual pin overrides (PM-77012). ENG to add verification stub that rejects unsigned manifests on Private deploys. Security to produce key-rotation schedule.
